exercise.name: Kneeling Leg Half Circle

reference.title: Kneeling Leg Half Circle (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (hip extension and abduction, straight leg)

breathing.pattern: Exhale through the arc out, inhale through the arc back.

prescription.tempo: About 2 s out, 1 s pause, 2 s back
prescription.progression: Ankle weight, then a mini band above the knees

cues.text: On all fours: hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat, neck long.
Straighten the right leg behind you, toes pointed just above the mat.
Breathe out and sweep the straight leg up and out to the side in a half circle, toes ending just off the mat out to the side.
Breathe in and trace the same half circle back behind you.
Bend the knee back under the hip; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Trunk swaying and hips tilting with the leg
mistakes.fix: Brace; the pelvis stays level and square, only the leg moves.
Keep the leg long from hip to toes.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back at the top of the arc
mistakes.fix: Keep the arc low enough that the back stays flat.
Slow, even half circle in about 2 s each way.

kinematics.norm: Hands under the shoulders, support knee under the hip (clinical opinion)
Straight leg extended behind to about hip height without lumbar extension (clinical opinion)
Leg carried out to the side within a comfortable range (clinical opinion)
Slow and even, about 2 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #469312, Kneeling Leg Half Circle (male), video (movement reference)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)
Macadam, Cronin & Contreras 2015, gluteal muscle activity in dynamic hip abduction and hip external rotation exercise: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 10(5):573-591; PMC4595911)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a mat or folded towel under the knees.
modify: Wrist discomfort: fists or forearms on the mat.
Low back or hip discomfort: make the arc smaller.
progressions: Pause at the top of the arc.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the straight leg extended behind the hip; quadruped hip extension with the knee extending gave about 29% MVIC in the superior gluteus maximus (Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Carries the leg out to the side through the arc (hip abduction); Boren 2011 measured about 57% MVIC gluteus medius in standing hip circumduction, the closest studied movement.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension with the knee straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Support side: keeps the pelvis level on three points (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still while the leg circles (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pelvis rotating toward the moving leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pelvis rotating toward the moving leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the support arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the support arms (clinical opinion).
